category_title: Students with aggressive behaviors and impulse control difficulties in urban environments
minimal_context: Dominic is observing the newly hatched chicks during independent project work and painting a picture for them.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Dominic, it is time for independent project work. You can observe the chicks.

STUDENT: I want to paint for them. Can I use some special metallic paints from the storage cabinet?

TUTOR: Here are the metallic paints. What are you going to do with your painting?

STUDENT: (Turns the painting over and places it picture-side-down on the cage) I am putting it like this so that the chicks can enjoy it.

TUTOR: Your classmate is coming over to look at the chicks with you.

STUDENT: No! Get away! (Hits the classmate) You can't look at them!

options.A: Walk across the room and stand behind the student during the independent project work.
options.B: Grant access to the special metallic paints from storage to support the student's creative initiative.
options.C: Provide help in the form of giving the student specific instructions for solving peer conflicts.
options.D: Redirect the student to the painting task quickly and emphasize the importance of staying focused.
